claim: Across independent evaluations, LLMs exhibit substantially lower and less human-aligned personalization performance on human or realistic long-horizon data than on synthetic or simplified setups, including cases where humans rate ‘personalized’ outputs no better than generic ones.

evidence.quote: generate personalized responses that humans judge no better than generic responses (though that LLM judges widely rate as better).

Results indicate that LLM performance significantly drops as context length grows and preference expression becomes more implicit, and that generalizing user preference understanding to unseen scenarios poses further challenges.

prediction.claim: By 2027-06-30, at least one new human-evaluated personalization study will report that a state-of-the-art LLM’s personalized responses are preferred by human raters in less than 60% of cases over generic responses on a human- or long-horizon-based dataset.
prediction.checkable: A published human evaluation shows <60% human preference for personalized vs. generic responses for at least one SOTA LLM on a human/long-horizon personalization benchmark.

refutation_condition: If independent evaluations using human conversations or long-horizon realistic contexts show no material drop relative to synthetic/simplified setups (e.g., humans prefer personalized outputs >75% of the time and relevance selection aligns within ~5% of human judgments), the claim is false.
